newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk central bank says now to stop issuing all CDs.
newsitem.headline: Turk central bank says now to stop issuing all CDs.

text.p: Turkey's central bank said on Wednesday that it decided to stop issuing all certificates of deposit (CDs) as part of Turkish efforts to counter money laundering.
The bank said earlier that it would only stop issuing CDs to unidentified customers, but it later said in a corrected statement that it would cease all issues.
"According to the decision taken by the Turkish Republic Central Bank counci, the practice of issuing certificates of deposit will cease completely," the statement said.
Earlier, the bank said the decision was taken at a council meeting on January 28.
The earlier statement said a government meeting last August included the issue of a customer's identity among proposals to combat money laundering.

The new regulation will become effective after a related central bank decree is published in the country's Official Gazette and existing certificates will remain valid until expiry, the statement said.
Turkey's parliament passed a law aimed at curbing money laundering in November as part of a fight against organised crime, particularly drug smuggling.
The law envisaged the creation of an authority to investigate financial crimes which would pass on its findings to public prosecutors.
